title: Lesson 90: Final Synthesis: The Enterprise AI Architect's Toolkit, Complete
description: Tests the four-shelf toolkit sort, the difference between a capability limit and an enforced control, the seam that explains an unapproved action, and the rule for choosing two deep areas as an accountable architect.

questions.question: A reviewer asks the architect whether an agent can email a customer on its own. One answer names an instruction the model can decline, and the other names a control. Which of these is a control rather than a capability limit?
options: A sentence in the system prompt that tells the agent never to email the customer directly
A deny rule that blocks the send tool
A named on-call owner recorded in the runbook
A quarterly re-label of the held-out evaluation set
questions.explanation: The lesson separates a capability limit, which is an instruction the model can decline on any given run, from a control, which holds regardless of what the model decides. A deny rule that blocks the send tool is enforced outside the model, while the prompt line is only a request. The runbook owner and the re-label cadence are real audit items, but neither one stops the action.

questions.question: An agent's reply sits at the draft-only rung, meaning a human should send everything, yet the incident log keeps filling with sends nobody approved. Which seam does the lesson tell you to check first?
options: The evaluation set against retrieval freshness
The cost envelope against the evaluation suite
The autonomy rung against the credential scope
The governance policy against the enforced control
questions.explanation: The lesson names this seam as the one that turns a bounded design into an unbounded one: an action at the draft-only rung is still an action if the credential behind it can write. The scope is the real permission, and it is usually set in a console the design document never mentions. Freshness, cost and policy are the other three seams, and none of them explains an unauthorized send.

questions.question: You are the accountable architect for an agent that is already in production and you are picking the two areas you will go deep on. What does the lesson require of those two areas?
options: One of your two areas must come from the control shelf.
Both of your areas must come from the shelf with the nearest failure.
Your areas must be the newest protocol and the newest evaluation tool.
Both of your areas must come from the build shelf.
questions.explanation: The deep areas are chosen by exposure and visibility, then one constraint is applied to accountability: one of your two areas must come from the control shelf, because that is the shelf where being a generalist gets expensive. The lesson also insists that a deep area without an artifact within thirty days is a reading list. Novelty is named as the wrong basis for the choice.
